add.title: World Report 2024: Mexico | Human Rights Watch
add.summary: HRW World Report 2024, Mexico chapter: documents Mexico's national legal-gender-recognition framework (administrative name/gender-marker changes on birth certificates in 21 of 32 states, a 2019 Supreme Court ruling setting LGR standards, extended to adolescents and children in March 2022). Its SOGI section covers marriage and document-level recognition only and contains no information on where transgender prisoners are housed in Oaxaca or in Mexico generally.

add.title: Trans Rights in Mexico: Progress and Challenges | Human Rights Watch
add.summary: HRW's state-by-state map documents that Oaxaca created an administrative legal-gender-recognition procedure in 2019, extended it to children 12 and older in 2021, and saw a June 2023 Supreme Court ruling reopen access for children under 12. As with Veracruz, the page contains no prison-placement data: Oaxaca's only documented gender-identity law concerns identity documents, not where trans inmates are held.
